record_scope_reconstruction: Merauke order covers Sota, Kali Torasi and Bupul people crossings; a separate overlapping phase confirms Sota traditional cross-border access remained restricted. Domestic tourism at the new PLBN grounds is not international reopening.

source_checks.finding: Original March report identifies all three crossings and explicitly locates the Sota gate at PLBN Sota.
Jubi October 15 confirms traditional Sota crossing remains closed while discussing future twice-weekly shopping permission.
Sota border-control grounds outline was mapped in May 2020; crossing-area reference only.

sites.name: Sota Indonesian border post
sites.coordinate_method: Mean of unique vertices in fresh OSM named feature outline
sites.precision: Representative point within the named border-post grounds, about 300 m; not an exact barrier
sites.evidence_note: Named Sota Border area explicitly tagged border_control, connected to Jalan Akses PLBNT Sota. The named 2024 BNPP service order identifies this Indonesian post, not Sota village or a PNG counterpart.

phase_decisions.phase_applicability: Merauke order covers Sota, Kali Torasi and Bupul people crossings; a separate overlapping phase confirms Sota traditional cross-border access remained restricted. Domestic tourism at the new PLBN grounds is not international reopening.

date_scope_check.finding: Geography review only. Current phase bounds, traffic exceptions, uncertain onset, reopening status and >24-hour decision are retained; current map features are not evidence of historical operation.
date_scope_check.qualification:
R6-EA-006-R1: Last substantive observation is March 19; March 20 publication does not extend it. Not reopening, not continuity to December or 2022.

R6-EA-006-REV1: Sota only; overlaps the Sota portion of R6-EA-006-R1 and must not be added arithmetically to it. October 15 is last confirmation, not reopening. Later twice-weekly shopping entry existed by December 29; first permission date unresolved.

Partial later access: a 29 December 2020 interview reports 15–20 nearby PNG residents already shopping at Sota twice weekly. This bounds the Sota shopping restriction by that date; the first permitted shopping day remains unknown. It does not establish reopening at Kali Torasi or Bupul or all-person daily entry at Sota. A planned renewed January 2021 ban is a separate episode.

unresolved: Kali Torasi and Bupul exact control sites remain unverified.
